subject: MSA / Order Form - security exhibit: triggered evidence windows & pen-test guardrails
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma@helixhealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: security exhibit — proposed evidence windows and pen test guardrails

Hi Grace / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we start to align on the MSA and Order Form, security has a few asks that we want captured in the security exhibit and order form language so our procurement and infosec teams can sign off. High level:

- Triggered evidence windows: we need clarity on what triggers an inspection (annual review, breach, regulatory request) and an approximate SLA for handing over SOC2 artifacts and logs.
- Pen test guardrails: Helix requires a staging window, scoped IP ranges, and a 72-hour notice for any intrusive tests; also, we want a requirement that the vendor provide a point-of-contact and a short plan for impact mitigation.
- SOC 2 mapping: list of which SOC2 artifacts Redwood will provide (audit report, control mappings, monitoring evidence).

I've attached a short RFI and our pen test requirements doc for reference. Can you propose wording we can put in an MSA exhibit and a suggested evidence cadence (monthly/quarterly) for SOC2 artifacts?

Proposed attendees for a quick 30-min sync: Grace, Laura, Karthik, plus our security ops lead Ryan. We can be flexible this week.

Attachments: Helix_Security_RFI.xlsx (spreadsheet), Helix_PenTest_Requirements.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Emma Carter
Legal & Security Liaison
Helix Health

---

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Carter <emma@helixhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: security exhibit — proposed evidence windows and pen test guardrails

Emma —

Appreciate the clear ask. Quick internal summary and proposal below. I attached a one-page exhibit redline to illustrate the language.

1) Triggers: we propose three discrete triggers: (A) annual compliance request (scheduled), (B) regulatory/legal notice, (C) confirmed security incident affecting Helix data. For (A) we commit to provide the standard SOC2 report and control evidence within 10 business days of request (or earlier if previously uploaded to the shared folder). For (B) and (C) we propose a 5 business day evidence SLA with an option to escalate to a 48-hour bridge call for high-priority items.

2) Pen test guardrails: Redwood is comfortable with a staging-only pen-test requirement for tests that target customer workloads. We can accept 72-hour notice and scoped IP ranges, but we need an agreed blast radius (IPs/tenants) and a clear rollback/mitigation point-of-contact (we will supply a 24/7 oncall for the test window). Redwood requests that Helix share a short test plan 5 business days in advance so we can validate no production impact.

3) Evidence cadence: propose monthly SOC2 artifact uploads to a read-only shared drive for ongoing monitoring (logs / exception summaries), and quarterly packaged reports for formal review. For triggered inspections, we will provide a scoped artifact bundle (per trigger) within the SLA above.

Next steps: can we lock a 30-min call tomorrow 08:30-11:00 PT? If legal wants to propose exact clause text I can route that to our legal and security partners for signoff.

Attachments: proposed_exhibit_redlines.docx

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Emma Carter <emma@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: security exhibit — proposed evidence windows and pen test guardrails

On Mon, Jul 21, 2025 at 11:03 AM grace.oconnor@redwood.ai wrote:
> 1) Triggers: we propose three discrete triggers: (A) annual compliance request (scheduled), (B) regulatory/legal notice, (C) confirmed security incident affecting Helix data....

Emma / team —

Thanks Grace — I reviewed the proposed exhibit redlines. A few legal comments and a suggested tightened clause set so the MSA remains scalable across customers:

- Inspection trigger language: we can accept (A)-(C) but recommend adding an objective threshold for (C) to avoid ambiguous "confirmed" language — propose: "material unauthorized access to Helix Health data confirmed by Redwood or an independent assessor".
- Notice windows: for scheduled annual reviews we will keep 10 business days. For incident-driven requests we propose 5 business days to supply evidence, but we will limit live on-prem or privileged inspection to a maximum of two such inspections per 12-month period unless mutually agreed.
- Pen test wording: substitute "staging-only" with "non-production isolated test environment" and require a high-level test plan 5 business days prior. For intrusive tests that could impact multi-tenant infrastructure we will require joint operational coordination and a pre-agreed safe-word.

I attached a clean redline doc with clause references. If Helix legal can accept these edits we can fold into the Order Form exhibit and issue a DocuSign for the Order Form.

DocuSign link for Order Form preview: https://www.docusign.com/OrderForm/HHL-2025-09

Attachments: redlines_clean.docx

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Carter <emma@helixhealth.com>, security-ops@helixhealth.com
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form: security exhibit — proposed evidence windows and pen test guardrails

Emma / Ryan —

Thank you for the RFI and the patience while we reviewed. Summary of the internal position and a proposed compromise to keep procurement moving:

- Accepted: scheduled annual evidence (10 business days), monthly SOC2 artifact feed to a read-only folder, and requirement for a 5-business-day notice for incident evidence bundles.

- Counterproposal on inspections: Redwood cannot agree to unlimited on-site or privileged inspections for incident requests. Instead we propose: (a) up to two incident-triggered inspection windows per 12-month period (as Karthik suggested); (b) for higher-severity incidents we will engage an independent third-party assessor to produce a scoped report within 15 business days if Helix requests an independent validation; (c) we will provide a 2-hour bridge within 48 hours of any pen-test that impacts shared infra to review findings and mitigation steps.

- Pen-tests: we accept Helix's 72-hour notice and scoped IP ranges for tests against the customer-isolated staging environment. We will provide a named POC and an incident-contact sheet. We would ask that Helix limit intrusive tests to a single 8-hour window per engagement to reduce cross-customer risk, with an option for a follow-up window if mutually agreed.

Proposed timeline / next steps:
1) Helix legal to review the attached redlines_clean.docx and confirm acceptance or mark exceptions by EOD Fri 25 Jul.
2) If accepted, Redwood legal will incorporate into the Order Form exhibit and issue the DocuSign preview (link above).
3) Security teams to run a 30-min bridge call if Helix wants to walk through the pen-test guardrails (suggest 26 Jul 10:00 PT).

I pasted the key exhibit language we intend to add at the bottom of this message for quick scanning.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Manager, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redlines_clean.docx

- "Pen Test Guardrails: Customer-initiated testing must be executed against an isolated non-production environment, with a high-level test plan provided 5 business days prior, a 72-hour notice for the test window, and a named Redwood POC available during the engagement. Intrusive tests impacting multi-tenant infrastructure must be jointly coordinated and will be limited to an initial 8-hour window unless otherwise agreed."
